headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection and cascading-error from a browser-facing auth proxy into a prompt-leak corpus; no direct shared channel is documented, so most risks remain bounded.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Authelia can sit in front of web content via ForwardAuth and broad network egress, but system_prompts_leaks has no documented ingestion path or shared channel. The pairwise injection pathway is therefore not provably absent, yet it appears to require unusual manual bridging rather than default interaction.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies Authelia-protected web output into system_prompts_leaks inputs, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added, the pathway strengthens.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable any manual copy-paste bridge between them during review.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on any shared channel.
requires-engineering: enforce content sanitization before downstream parsing.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Authelia touches no data classes in the profile and system_prompts_leaks also lists no data classes touched. With no shared workspace, OAuth principal, or file-transfer surface documented, there is no plausible pairwise leakage pathway to sensitive data in the provided profiles.
conditions: IF either agent is later configured to process sensitive files in a shared workspace, reassess leakage.
IF a common OAuth principal is introduced, reassess leakage.
mitigations: Keep sensitive data out of both agents' inputs.
Use separate OS users or containers.
Review any future shared storage mount before enabling it.
requires-engineering: add access controls and audit logging on shared data paths.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress but no filesystem write or subprocess capability, while system_prompts_leaks has no documented write, network, or concurrency surface. The profiles do not show overlapping mutable-resource access, so capability conflict is not plausible from the documented pair.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory, reassess conflict.
IF either agent gains git or database write scopes, reassess conflict.
mitigations: Avoid mounting a shared writable directory.
Keep git operations outside both agents.
Document any future shared mutable resource before enabling it.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Authelia can produce authentication decisions or forwarded responses, but system_prompts_leaks is a source-available corpus with no documented action-taking authority. The pair does not show a default pipeline where B blindly acts on A's output, so cascading error is limited unless an operator wires them together manually.
conditions: IF system_prompts_leaks is configured to treat Authelia output as authoritative text, cascading error increases.
IF B is connected to an action-taking downstream system, reassess severity.
mitigations: Insert a human verification step before reuse of A's output.
Label A's output as untrusted in any downstream workflow.
Keep B read-only unless explicitly reviewed.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for any A-to-B handoff.

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either agent. Authelia is open-source and system_prompts_leaks is source-available, but the profiles do not show regulated data classes or jurisdictional constraints, so a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into either agent, reassess compliance.
IF deployment jurisdiction or retention policy is specified later, reassess compliance.
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data through either agent.
Record deployment jurisdiction and retention settings.
Review any future privacy policy before enabling data flow.
requires-engineering: implement retention and deletion controls if regulated data is added.
